sentences.text: Prerna Mathpal vs Shubham Loshali on 11 November, 2024

Bench: J.K. Maheshwari, Rajesh Bindal
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition (Civil) No. 1327 Of 2024
 Prerna Mathpal  Petitioner(S)
 Versus
 Shubham Loshali  Respondent(S)
 Order

1. The present petition has been filed by Petitioner-Wife seeking transfer of Original Civil Suit bearing No. 06 of 2024 titled as Shubham Loshali vs. Prerna Mathpal filed by Respondent- Husband for restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
2. On 25.09.2024, when this case was listed before this Court, it was informed that a settlement has been arrived at between the parties.

On 21.10.2024 it was submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that in pursuance to the settlement, parties have filed a joint application vide I.A. No.
244597 under Article 142 of the Constitution of India seeking divorce by mutual consent and prayed for appropriate directions.

3. Upon settlement a petition was filed jointly by the petitioner and respondent before the Court of Ld. Principal Judge, Family courts, District East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi, in H.M.A. Petition No.1797/2024, the parties have settled the following terms:
A. That petitioner no. 2 (Shubham Loshali) shall pay a sum of Rs.9,00,000/-
(Rupees Nine Lakh Only) as full and final settlement towards her dowry and stridhan articles as well as towards the maintenance (past, present and future) qua this marriage in three installments and the parties would approach for dissolution of marriage by way of filing petition u/s 13-B(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and second motion u/s 13-B(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 shall be filed after 20 days of the decision/order in a petition U/s 13-B(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
B.

entities.text: Court of Ld. Principal Judge, Family courts, District East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: That it has been further agreed between the parties that out of the settled amount, an amount of Rs. 4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakh Only) shall be paid by petitioner no. 2 (Shubham Loshali) to petitioner no. 1 (Prerna Mathpal) by way of RTGS/IMPS/Demand Draft at the time of recording of Prerna Mathpal vs Shubham Loshali on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118508468/
1 statement of first motion U/s 13-B (1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

C. That it is further agreed between the parties that the petitioner no. 2 shall pay the second installment of Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only) to petitioner no. 1 at the time of recording of statement of the second motion U/s 13-B (2) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 by way of RTGS/IMPS/Demand Draft which would be filed after 20 days from the date of decision on petition U/s 13-B (1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 with a waiver application.
D. That it is further agreed between the parties that the petitioner no. 2 shall pay the third installment (i.e., the remaining amount out of the final settlement amount of Rs. 9,00,000/-
(Rupees Nine Lakh Only) of Rs. 4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakh Only) to petitioner no. 1 at the time of quashing of FIR bearing no. 323/2024 U/s 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 registered at P.S.: New Ashok Nagar, Delhi before the Hon'ble Delhi High Court by way of RTGS/IMPS/Demand Draft which would be filed within 20 days from the date of decision/decree on petition U/s 13-B (2) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
E.

That it is has already been agreed between the parties that all the payments as in to the settlement amount of Rs. 9,00,000/- (Rupees Nine Lakh Only) shall be received by petitioner no. 1 and be paid by petitioner no. 2 to petitioner no. I in the name of Sh. Hari Dutt Mathpal in Bank Account No.:
628501502161 Bank: ICICI Bank bearing IFSC No. ICIC0006285 by way of RTGS/IMPS/Demand Draft.

It is also not out of place to mention here that the petitioner no. 1 undertakes not to raise any adverse claim as to receiving the said payment in the name and bank account of the father of petitioner no. 1 i.e., Sh. Hari Dutt Mathpal in future against petitioner no. 2.
F.

That it has also been agreed between the parties that the gold articles (pertaining to dowry and stridhan articles of petitioner no. 1) shall be returned to petitioner no. 1 by petitioner no. 2 on or a day before recording of the statement of the second motion U/s 13-B (2) of the Hindu Marriage Act,
1955 alongwith the monetary payment of the second installment to the tune of Rs. 1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh Only) as mentioned hereinabove.

G. That it has also been agreed between the parties that the gold articles (pertaining to petitioner no.
2) shall be returned to petitioner no. 2 by petitioner no. 1 on or a day before recording of the statement of the second motion U/s 13-B (2) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 alongwith payment of the second installment to the tune of Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only) as mentioned hereinabove.

H. That it has already been agreed between both the parties that the other material articles lying at the matrimonial home of petitioner no. 1 bearing Ward No. 56, Manpur East, Rampur Road,
Haldwani-263139 District Nainital, Uttarakhand shall be returned to petitioner no. 1 by petitioner no. 2 after recording of statement recording of statement of first motion U/s 13-B (1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 at Haldwani in presence of both the parties with their respective Counsels.

I. That it has already been agreed between the parties that the pending litigations as mentioned hereinabove shall be withdrawn by the respective parties after recording of statement of first motion Prerna Mathpal vs Shubham Loshali on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118508468/
2 for attaining decree for dissolution of marriage U/s 13-B (1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

J. That it is further agreed between the parties that they will withdraw any other complaint/case filed by/against either of the parties or their family members in any other court in Delhi/Haldwani/India after recording of statement of first motion for attaining decree for dissolution of marriage U/s 13-B (1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

K. That it is also agreed between the parties that all the matters emanating from this marriage civil or criminal are settled and neither of the parties nor their relatives shall make any claim against each other at any time in future in any court of law/police station or any other place.
L.

That it is also agreed between the parties that either of the parties if commit breach or default of this mutually agreed settlement after the recording of the first motion, if the wife i.e., petitioner no. 1 backs out, the amount taken at the time of first motion shall be returned to petitioner no. 2 with an interest @2% per month and in case the husband i.e., petitioner no. 2 backs out, the amount given at the time of the first motion shall stand forfeited by petitioner no. 1, it is further understood by the parties that for the breach of undertaking given to the concerned Ld. Court of wilful/deliberate violation of a consent order/decree, the defaulting party will be liable to be punished for the Contempt of Court.
M. That it is further agreed between the parties that they shall remain bound with the aforesaid terms and conditions as mentioned hereinabove.

It is not out of place to mention here that the abovesaid settlement terms have been arrived at between the parties voluntarily out of their own free will and consent and without there being any undue pressure, force, coercion, undue influence,
misrepresentation or mistake and the parties have agreed that the settlement has been correctly recorded as per the agreed terms and conditions.
4. As per the settlement, it is stated that civil cases pending between the parties may be disposed of and FIR registered against the respondent may be quashed.

5. As per settlement, the respondent has to pay a sum of 9,00,000/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs only) to the petitioner and all the payments as in to the settlement amount of 9,00,000/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Only) shall be received by petitioner and be paid by respondent to petitioner towards past,
present and future maintenance and permanent alimony.
It is also agreed that after receipt of the said amount, she will not claim any right in any property of the husband or of his family.
6. We have perused the joint application by which the parties have settled their dispute.
We have interacted with the petitioner and the respondent who are present in the Court via video conferencing and have been identified by their respective Advocates.
7. During hearing, the parties have acknowledged the terms of the settlement.

The petitioner states that in terms of the settlement, she has received all the dowry articles and the sum of 9,00,000/-
(Rupees Nine Lakhs only).
Both the parties have requested that in view of settlement, decree of divorce by mutual consent may be passed.

Prerna Mathpal vs Shubham Loshali on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118508468/
3 8.

Having heard learned counsel as also the parties and considering the terms of settlement and the joint application filed, we are of the view that the settlement deserves to be accepted and accordingly, we dispose of this transfer petition including the joint application with the following directions:
(i) The petitioner (wife) has received a sum of 9,00,000/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs only)
in lieu of past, present and future permanent alimony and she will not claim any right or interest in the property of the respondent (husband) and/or his family.

(ii) Restitution Petition filed by the Respondent- husband under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 bearing number Original Civil Suit No.06 of 2024 titled Shubham Loshali v. Prerna Mathpal pending before the Family Courts, Haldwani,
Nainital, Uttarakhand is disposed of.
(iii) Petition filed by Petitioner-wife for maintenance under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. pending before the Family Court, District East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi is disposed of.

entities.text: Family Court, District East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: (iv) FIR No.323/2024 u/s 498A/406/34 of IPC registered at P.S. New Ashok Nagar, Delhi, is quashed.

(v) Accepting the terms of settlement and as consented by the parties, we grant decree of divorce by mutual consent in exercise of our power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India and declare the marriage solemnized between the petitioner and the respondent on 10.02.2023 as dissolved and they are at liberty to live their lives with free will independently without any interruption.
9.
The settlement be treated to be a part of this order and the parties shall abide by the same.
10. Decree-sheet be prepared.
11. Information of this order be sent to the Courts concerned for necessary action.
12. Ordered accordingly.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

., J.
[ J.K. MAHESHWARI ] ., J.
[ RAJESH BINDAL ] New Delhi November 11, 2024.
